124|     """The ``JSONLIterator`` is used to iterate over JSON-encoded objects
125|     stored in the `JSON Lines format`_ (one object per line).
126| 
127|     Most notably it has the ability to efficiently read from the
128|     bottom of files, making it very effective for reading in simple
129|     append-only JSONL use cases. It also has the ability to start from
130|     anywhere in the file and ignore corrupted lines.
131| 
132|     Args:
133|         file_obj (file): An open file object.
134|         ignore_errors (bool): Whether to skip over lines that raise an error on
135|             deserialization (:func:`json.loads`).
136|         reverse (bool): Controls the direction of the iteration.
137|             Defaults to ``False``. If set to ``True`` and *rel_seek*
138|             is unset, seeks to the end of the file before iteration
139|             begins.
140|         rel_seek (float): Used to preseek the start position of
141|             iteration. Set to 0.0 for the start of the file, 1.0 for the
142|             end, and anything in between.
143| 
144|     .. _JSON Lines format: http://jsonlines.org/
145|     """
146|     def __init__(self, file_obj,
147|                  ignore_errors=False, reverse=False, rel_seek=None):
148|         self._reverse = bool(reverse)
149|         self._file_obj = file_obj
150|         self.ignore_errors = ignore_errors
151| 
152|         if rel_seek is None:
153|             if reverse:
154|                 rel_seek = 1.0
155|         elif not -1.0 < rel_seek < 1.0:
156|             raise ValueError("'rel_seek' expected a float between"
157|                              " -1.0 and 1.0, not %r" % rel_seek)
158|         elif rel_seek < 0:
159|             rel_seek = 1.0 + rel_seek
160|         self._rel_seek = rel_seek
161|         self._blocksize = 4096
162|         if rel_seek is not None:
163|             self._init_rel_seek()
164|         if self._reverse:
165|             self._line_iter = reverse_iter_lines(self._file_obj,
166|                                                  blocksize=self._blocksize,
167|                                                  preseek=False)
168|         else:
169|             self._line_iter = iter(self._file_obj)
170| 
171|     @property
172|     def cur_byte_pos(self):
173|         "A property representing where in the file the iterator is reading."
174|         return self._file_obj.tell()
175| 
176|     def _align_to_newline(self):
177|         "Aligns the file object's position to the next newline."
178|         fo, bsize = self._file_obj, self._blocksize
179|         cur, total_read = '', 0
180|         cur_pos = fo.tell()
181|         while '\n' not in cur:
182|             cur = fo.read(bsize)
183|             if not cur:
184|                 # no newline until EOF; a partial trailing line was
185|                 # never yieldable from a mid-line seek anyway
186|                 fo.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
187|                 return
188|             total_read += bsize
189|         newline_offset = cur.index('\n') + total_read - bsize
190|         fo.seek(cur_pos + newline_offset)
191| 
192|     def _init_rel_seek(self):
193|         "Sets the file object's position to the relative location set above."
194|         rs, fo = self._rel_seek, self._file_obj
195|         if rs == 0.0:
196|             fo.seek(0, os.SEEK_SET)
197|         else:
198|             fo.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)
199|             size = fo.tell()
200|             if rs == 1.0:
201|                 self._cur_pos = size
202|             else:
203|                 target = int(size * rs)
204|                 fo.seek(target, os.SEEK_SET)
205|                 self._align_to_newline()
206|                 self._cur_pos = fo.tell()
207| 
208|     def __iter__(self):
209|         return self
210| 
211|     def next(self):
212|         """Yields one :class:`dict` loaded with :func:`json.loads`, advancing
213|         the file object by one line. Raises :exc:`StopIteration` upon reaching
214|         the end of the file (or beginning, if ``reverse`` was set to ``True``.
215|         """

FILES: boltons/jsonutils.py:155-157
ROOT CAUSE: The `JSONLIterator.__init__` method uses a strict inequality `not -1.0 < rel_seek < 1.0` to validate `rel_seek`, which rejects `1.0` even though it is documented as the end of the file and explicitly handled in `_init_rel_seek`.
CHANGE: Modify the validation check in `JSONLIterator.__init__` to allow `rel_seek` to be exactly `1.0`. Change `not -1.0 < rel_seek < 1.0` to `not -1.0 < rel_seek <= 1.0`.
TEST: tests/test_jsonutils.py
